item.text: {"text":"Closest precedents: [AttrFormer (KDD 2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3690624.3709267) models categorical and numerical attributes as explicit relations in sequential recommendation; [MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) learns multiple attribute-aware text representations and matches user interests to items at attribute level. These support learning structured attribute interactions beyond a single pooled text vector, but do not establish a scratch-trained encoder that preserves number–unit binding or connector direction. MARS uses pretrained language representations, so its implementation is outside the permitted setup. [2026 quantity-reasoning research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03982) also reports systematic number- and unit-specific shortcuts: text representations alone should not be assumed to understand physical quantities.\n\nExperiment hypothesis, rather than a demonstrated literature result: jointly train a compact positional token encoder inside the existing HSTU, using only permitted titles/descriptions. Preserve digits, decimals, unit case, punctuation, and ordered connector spans; contextualize tokens before pooling so “USB-C to HDMI” can differ from “HDMI to USB-C,” and “12 V” from “12 W.” Fuse the resulting representation with item-ID embeddings through a learned internal gate and optimize the entire network with next-item supervision. Keep one trained checkpoint per category and the HSTU backbone. Compare against pooled text under the fixed macro validation HR@10 protocol; use controlled text perturbations to check sensitivity to reversed connectors and changed quantities. Such sensitivity measures representation behavior, not verified product compatibility. The search found related attribute methods, but no direct evidence that this exact scratch-trained design improves the specified benchmark."}
